alignment.note: Greek articular pronoun ὁ (substantivised with δέ) is rendered in Syriac by the demonstrative ܗܘ and in Latin by ille; all three function as a resumptive subject pronoun marking the contrastive turn to Peter.
δέ / ܕܝܢ / At as adversative discourse marker; Latin fronts the conjunction At before the pronoun, an order difference of no semantic weight.

The participle λέγων ('saying') is matched by Syriac coordinated finite ܘܐܡܪ ('and said'), a typical Aramaic paratactic rendering of Greek participial syntax; the Vulgate dicens followed by the colon introduces direct speech.

Greek and Latin both preserve the emphatic double negative correlative οὔτε...οὔτε / Neque...neque with two distinct verbs ('I neither know nor understand'); the Peshitta compresses this to a single negated clause ܠܐ ܝܕܥ ܐܢܐ ('I do not know'), omitting the second verb ἐπίσταμαι and simplifying the rhetorical pleonasm.

The emphatic Greek pronoun σύ ('you yourself') has no separate counterpart in either version; the Syriac enclitic ܐܢܬܝ within the clause and the Latin second-person verb dicas carry the subject inflectionally, so the explicit pronoun is absorbed rather than independently rendered.
Interrogative τί / ܡܢܐ / quid introducing the indirect/relative question.

Greek λέγεις and Latin dicas express the second-person verb; the Peshitta uses participle ܐܡܪܐ with the feminine enclitic pronoun ܐܢܬܝ, agreeing in person but adding gendered specification absent from Greek and Latin.
Coordinating καί / ܘ (prefixed to ܢܦܩ) / Et.
Verb of departure ἐξῆλθεν / ܢܦܩ / exiit; the Syriac conjunction and verb are written as one orthographic token ܘܢܦܩ.
Adverb ἔξω ('out') / ܠܒܪ / foras reinforcing the verb of egress.

Greek εἰς τὸ προαύλιον ('into the forecourt/porch') and Latin ante atrium ('before the courtyard') employ a preposition plus noun for the gateway area; the Syriac renders this with the single noun ܠܣܦܐ ('to the vestibule/threshold'), a lexical choice for the entryway that collapses the prepositional phrase.
Coordinating καί / ܘ (prefixed to ܩܪܐ) / et.
Verb of crowing ἐφώνησεν / ܩܪܐ / cantavit; the Syriac uses the root q-r-a ('to call/cry out') for the cock's crow, fused with the conjunction in ܘܩܪܐ.
